title: Getting Started with timescapes
text: small example two periods presence condition separated absence condition. time step case represents year, first two years condition, two years absence, followed three years presence one year absence. values can visualized simple timeline.  Now, calculate metrics using ts_metric(), selecting available list metrics found using ts_list_metrics(). Time steps unitless ordered observations duration defined user. Gap metrics include leading trailing absence runs default. Set include_boundary_gaps = FALSE count gaps presence periods; qualifying gaps returns 0, including -absence series. core metrics, supply min_core_period, positive whole number time steps. presence run qualifies full length least threshold. core_time_index divides total length qualifying runs total presence time (0 presence); n_core_periods counts qualifying runs. Omitting threshold uses 15 time steps issues one warning per vector raster call. former core_buffer argument longer accepted. example: Every observed value must 0 1. series containing missing time step produces NA, removing reinterpreting step change temporal pattern.
code: library(timescapes)  x <- c(1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0) plot(   seq_along(x), x,   type = "s",   ylim = c(-0.1, 1.1),   xlab = "Time step",   ylab = "Habitat available",   yaxt = "n",   main = "Binary habitat availability through time" ) axis(2, at = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes"), las = 1) ts_list_metrics() #>  [1] "total_time"      "n_periods"       "gap_mean"        "gap_max"         #>  [5] "duration_sd"     "edge_density"    "autocorr"        "aggregation"     #>  [9] "core_time_index" "n_core_periods" ts_metric(x, "total_time") #> [1] 5 ts_metric(x, "n_periods") #> [1] 2 ts_metric(x, "gap_mean") #> [1] 1.5 ts_metric(x, "core_time_index", min_core_period = 3) #> [1] 0.6 ts_metric(x, "n_core_periods", min_core_period = 3) #> [1] 1 ts_metric(c(1, 1, NA, 0), "n_periods") #> [1] NA

title: Quantifying Temporal Structure Across Landscapes
text: Calculate one metric supplying exact name ts_list_metrics(): available metrics : total_time: number time steps presence n_periods: number distinct presence periods gap_mean: mean length absence periods gap_max: maximum length absence period duration_sd: variability presence-period lengths edge_density: proportion adjacent steps change state autocorr: lag-1 Pearson autocorrelation aggregation: proportion adjacent steps state core_time_index: proportion presence time qualifying core periods n_core_periods: number presence periods containing core time Metric names must match exactly. Inputs must non-empty numeric vectors containing 0, 1, NA. time step missing, metric NA.
code: library(timescapes)  x <- c(1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 0)  ts_list_metrics() ts_metric(x, "n_periods") ts_metric(x, "gap_mean") ts_metric(x, "core_time_index", min_core_period = 3)

title: Calculate a binary timescape metric — ts_metric
text: Let n number time steps, let occupied period maximal run ones, let gap maximal run zeros, including leading trailing runs default. include_boundary_gaps = FALSE, gaps presence periods count. qualifying gaps (including -zero series boundary gaps excluded) returns 0. total_time: sum series; range 0 n. n_periods: number occupied periods; range 0 ceiling(n / 2). gap_mean: arithmetic mean gap lengths, 0 gaps occur. gap_max: maximum gap length, 0 gaps occur. duration_sd: sample standard deviation occupied-period lengths, 0 fewer two occupied periods occur. edge_density: number changes adjacent time steps divided n - 1; returns 0 one-step series. autocorr: Pearson correlation steps 1 n - 1 steps 2 n; returns NA correlation undefined. aggregation: proportion adjacent time-step pairs equal; returns 0 one-step series. core_time_index: proportion occupied time presence runs whose full length least min_core_period; returns 0 presence occurs. n_core_periods: number qualifying presence runs. Time steps unitless ordered observations; duration user-defined.
